entry.title: Amy Nicola McBride Releases Fishtail Generative MIDI Instrument
entry.content:
KVR Audio | kvraudio.com | source

Utilizing music theory-based algorithmic rules instead of generative AI, this composition system creates complete, repeatable multi-section musical pieces. Available for iPhone, iPad, and Mac, the software generates MIDI data that must be sent to a receiving synthesizer or software instrument for sound production.

The tool features seven musical voices with independent routing, seven intonation systems including MPE support, and "Retained Takes" to compare or rearrange musical segments. It supports Ableton Link and offers both standard MIDI and experimental analogue-CV file exports. Introductory pricing is offered until September 9, 2026, at $4.99 for iOS and $14.99 for Mac.

entry.title: U&I Software Releases MetaSynth CTX 2.x and ArtMatic Designer CTX 2.x
entry.content:
KVR Audio | kvraudio.com | source

U&I Software has released updates for MetaSynth and ArtMatic Designer on macOS, introducing MetaSynth CTX 2.x and ArtMatic Designer CTX 2.x. MetaSynth updates include Spectrum Synth 2.0 with increased spectral resolution, a HiDef audio engine, and direct USB microphone recording. The release also adds nested project architectures and macOS Finder integration.

ArtMatic Designer CTX 2.x enhances its audio-visual synthesis environment with 48 kHz audio support and a text-based interface for synthesizer parameter editing. The update also increases the number of image-to-audio read patterns and adds 3D object editing capabilities for the companion Voyager application. Both products offer 21-day full-use trials.

entry.title: Parish Audio Releases Aethon Granular Transformation Engine
entry.content:
KVR Audio | kvraudio.com | source

Parish Audio has released Aethon, a granular transformation effect for Windows and macOS. The plugin captures incoming audio in real time and breaks it into grains that can be repositioned, scattered, reversed, or smoothed to create evolving textures, rhythmic pulses, and atmospheric movement.

The engine includes controls for grain size, density, jitter, and host-synchronized rate, alongside a "Freeze" function to hold and transform specific captured audio. Additional features include a finishing FX section for filtering and spatial processing, real-time granular visualization, and a collection of factory presets.

entry.title: U&I Software Releases MetaSynth CTX 2.x Update
entry.content:
KVR Audio | kvraudio.com | source

U&I Software has released MetaSynth CTX 2.x, an update to its image-to-audio standalone Digital Audio Workstation for macOS. The update features Spectrum Synth 2.0, which offers increased slice resolution for spectral analysis, and a HiDef Audio Engine designed for pure, uncompressed audio paths. New features also include quantized live Image Synth switching and a dynamic preset management system for better organization and recall.

The version 2.x architecture introduces nested projects, allowing users to house multiple presets and arrangements within a single unified project. Workflow improvements include macOS Finder drag-and-drop support, direct recording for USB microphones, and support for odd-meter looping. MetaSynth CTX 2.x is available for macOS at a price of $343.85.

entry.title: Remi Blaze Releases Clampit Free Mastering Limiter for macOS
entry.content:
KVR Audio | kvraudio.com | source

This free macOS 15.0+ mastering limiter is available in AU, VST3, and Standalone formats. It incorporates a "Constant Loudness" mechanism and loudness-matched bypass to allow for accurate parameter comparison without deceptive volume increases.

Controls include adjustable ceiling, release, and lookahead, alongside three knee profiles: Knock, Glue, and Clobber. The software also provides 4x polyphase IIR oversampling, BS.1770 K-weighted LUFS metering, and a simplified one-knob companion called Clampit Raw.

entry.title: Devproaudio Updates Reverside Plugin to v1.0.1
entry.content:
KVR Audio | kvraudio.com | source

Devproaudio has released version 1.0.1 of its Reverside 3D spatial reverb plugin. The update includes GPU rendering optimizations that reduce idle usage by 3–4X and improve UI responsiveness. It also resolves audio crackling during automation in Bitwig and Cubase, fixes memory leaks, and corrects stereo-to-mono output configurations.

Reverside uses a dual-engine algorithmic reverb and a 3D positioning system based on listener placement and spatial geometry. The v1.0.1 update allows for up to three simultaneous demo instances and includes a redesigned audio player on the developer's website. The plugin is available for $135/€120, with free access for select legacy SpinAudio and 2CAudio customers.

entry.title: Stemwire Releases Mica Synthesizer
entry.content:
KVR Audio | kvraudio.com | source

Stemwire has released Mica, a synthesizer plugin for macOS and Windows that combines experimental sound engines with standard synthesis controls. The instrument features four engine types—Braids, Plaits, Elements, and a two-operator FM engine—alongside a sub oscillator and a sample-based noise generator.

The plugin offers 14 modulation sources routable to 622 destinations, including three envelopes, three LFOs, and three drawable waveform oscillators. It also includes four re-orderable effect slots with 12 effect types, such as granular and resonator processors.

entry.content:
Bedroom Producers Blog | bedroomproducersblog.com | source | discussion

Shadaloo Audio DSP has transitioned its Density EQ plugin to a permanent free offering. The plugin is a four-band equalizer designed to shape the presence and weight of audio tracks, aiming to increase track scale and mix-readiness without introducing harmonic harshness or muddiness.

The decision to make the tool free is intended to increase accessibility and allow a wider range of users to test the plugin's capabilities. Density EQ is available in VST3 format.

entry.title: EDM Producers Call Out AI-Generated Music Passed Off as Human Art
entry.content:
Techmeme | theverge.com

Electronic dance music producers are identifying and exposing AI-generated tracks presented as human-made. As generative tools like Suno enable users to create songs with minimal effort, artists such as Max “H4RRIS” Harris and Nihil Young are calling out 'AI slop' to protect the authenticity of the genre and the livelihoods of human creators.

The movement responds to a growing culture of mistrust fueled by audio artifacts like vocal stuttering and persistent hissing. While AI music has achieved mainstream success on TikTok and the Billboard charts, producers argue that generative tools threaten human artistry and the clarity of musical styles.
